claims.text: Cover page reads: '2 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-002 / Defense Intelligence Reference Document / Acquisition Threat Support / Positron Aerospace Propulsion'.

Released copy runs 35 pages; internal chapter structure covers antimatter, positron air-breathing propulsion, the positron ramjet engine and its UAV, ramjet-assisted missile and single-stage reusable vehicle applications, and solid-core and gas-core positron rockets.

a.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: produced under the AAWSA/AAWSAP contract
edges.note: Tier 2, and the reason is worth stating. A full-text scan of this released DIRD on 23 August 2026 found NO occurrence of the programme name anywhere in the document - unlike 27 of the 32 scanned, whose inside cover names the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program explicitly. The link therefore rests on the DIA's 9 January 2018 list to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which enumerates it among the 38 reference products, and not on the document's own text.

b.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC

edges.label: commissioned via the BAASS prime contract
edges.note: Positronics Research LLC was an outside small business with no standing DIA relationship; its deliverable reached DIA through the AAWSAP prime contract held by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies. Tier 2 because the contractor name is redacted on the cover page under (b)(3):10 USC 424 and the subcontract itself has not been released.

edges.label: authored by
edges.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion' to 'Dr Gerald Smith, Positronics Research'. Smith is a Yale physics Ph.D., former Penn State physics department head, and developer of the Mark I portable antiproton trap for NASA JPL and the High Performance Antimatter Trap for NASA Marshall; the DIRD subject matter tracks his own NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts study on positron-propelled vehicles.

edges.label: series member
edges.note: Membership of the DIRD series is established by the released document itself: its cover page carries the Defense Intelligence Reference Document mark and the DIA Defense Futures banner. Publication date 2 March 2010 on the cover. 36 pages in the released copy. The cover of the scanned release is degraded, so a document number or date is asserted here only where it reads unambiguously.

title: Released DIRD, 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion' — FOIA copy, cover page read 22 August 2026
